title: Build a world that defeats a rule
core_gate: Distinguish four color/shape types; understand every, some and not; give witnesses and a complete four-type argument. Count at most two objects.
index_gate: Every/some language; witness objects and a complete four-type argument
extension_gate: The arrow-world extension requires coordinating two quantifiers, without symbolic first-order notation.
assessment: First-pilot candidate with oral facilitation. Quantifier language is the real gate; stop before the last page if every/some remain unstable.
satisfying_stop: A smallest counterworld plus a four-type explanation of which claims are forced.

title: Can your list catch my pattern?
core_gate: Track row/position labels and give one guaranteed disagreement per row. Count to sixteen; symbolic algebra is unnecessary.
index_gate: Position matching and mismatch proofs; infinity is a separate advanced page
extension_gate: Final page: infinite sequences indexed by positive integers and a proof about an arbitrary enumeration. Finite play does not establish this readiness.
assessment: First-pilot candidate for finite escape. The infinity page is advanced/specialist; changing four counters is not itself an uncountability proof.
satisfying_stop: A missing word with four mismatch certificates and a method valid against every four-row list.

title: A collection with no card inside another
core_gate: Distinguish containment from overlap; count sixteen cards; use a chain partition as an upper bound.
index_gate: Set containment, counting to sixteen, and a chain-cover upper bound
extension_gate: Five-symbol extension: permutations, factorial counting and fractions, or an independently built ten-chain certificate.
assessment: First-pilot candidate after containment is secure. Chain construction may need a delayed hint; the proof is the mathematical destination.
satisfying_stop: Six chosen cards with a complete six-chain upper-bound certificate.

title: Send a network in a tiny message
core_gate: Recognize trees and leaves; follow changing smallest-label choices; explain why decoding is forced. Ordering labels through five and counting occurrences.
index_gate: Leaves, changing labels, and inverse reasoning; general n uses induction
extension_gate: General n proof uses induction and the degree/occurrence invariant; powers enter the final count.
assessment: Promising with specific gates. Changing graph/message state is demanding. The degree invariant, rather than a catalog of pictures, is the destination.
satisfying_stop: A successful exchange plus the reason absent message labels are exactly the current leaves.

title: How many connecting networks survive?
core_gate: Distinguish a connected minimal network from one with a cycle; count small cases and prove a complete classification by a choice of edges.
index_gate: Connectedness and complete case counts; determinants are separately gated
extension_gate: Page 4 requires matrices and 3-by-3 determinants. The general Matrix-Tree theorem is supplied there; proving it requires incidence matrices and Cauchy–Binet.
assessment: First-pilot candidate for the exact count and closure surprise. The determinant page is advanced/specialist and not needed to make the core substantial.
satisfying_stop: Eight classified trees, then a proof that closing a perimeter road destroys more of these choices than closing the diagonal.

title: Do two calculation routes agree?
core_gate: Follow upward comparisons, distinguish a least upper bound from any upper bound, and evaluate nested operations. No arithmetic; 0 and 1 are names.
index_gate: Least/greatest bounds and nested operations; no arithmetic required
extension_gate: General set identity uses membership reasoning. Subspace continuation needs linear algebra. The core counterexample requires neither.
assessment: Promising with specific gates. The five-tile diagram is compact, but least/greatest and nested operations are abstract; tangible result markers are essential. The final repair is optional depth.
satisfying_stop: Two well-defined calculation routes end at different elements in the five-element diamond, with a justified intermediate step at every operation.

title: Everything your starting clues force
core_gate: Follow visible positive if-then rules without deleting tokens; reason about forced additions, all possible orders and intersections. Count up to four tokens.
index_gate: Positive if-then rules and reasoning about every completed run
extension_gate: General finite proof uses induction on additions. A lattice-of-closed-sets explanation requires containment and least/greatest bounds, developed in AD-06.
assessment: First-pilot candidate for combining finished collections; promising with specific gates for the order-independence proof. Distinguish “no new token can be added” from merely choosing not to use an available rule.
satisfying_stop: Two completed collections combine to force a new token, and a least-closed-set argument explains why every completed run has the same outcome.

title: Which numbers may share a name?
core_gate: Use addition on a four-position ring or supplied table; choose representatives independently; prove a classification by translating identified pairs. Small sums and parity.
index_gate: Addition on a four-ring, independent representatives, and pair translation
extension_gate: Six-ring classification requires cyclic translation and subgroup/coset reasoning or a separately checked finite case argument.
assessment: Promising with specific gates. Independent representative choices and the pair-translation proof are substantial; parity familiarity alone is not the payoff.
satisfying_stop: All three valid renamings of addition modulo four, proved by translating an identified pair, with a concrete failure witness for an invalid renaming.

title: Can both schedules be right?
core_gate: Remainders, counting to twenty-four, ordered pairs and a completeness argument. Moving counters is the entry; compatibility and uniqueness within a period are the core.
index_gate: Remainders and paired clocks; gcd and Bézout are a separate advanced proof
extension_gate: General theorem: gcd, lcm, integer divisibility and a supplied Bézout identity. Three-clock continuation uses repeated congruence solving.
assessment: Promising with specific remainder gates. Test whether learners can hold two clock roles fixed; the general theorem is advanced number theory.
satisfying_stop: Classify every compatible four/six report pair and explain both the parity obstruction and why each compatible pair has one answer per twelve-minute period.

title: Can the next match hide between our answers?
core_gate: Figurate counting is the entry. The satisfying new core uses polynomial expansion, a two-variable recurrence, integer parity and positive-integer descent. Keep row count separate from square side.
index_gate: Algebra and integer descent for completeness; counter arrangements are an earlier entry
extension_gate: General Pell theory is not assumed. A recurrence for the matching totals uses algebra and second differences; optional exact calculator arithmetic is permitted.
assessment: Advanced/specialist for the satisfying proof; the counter entry is a promising earlier activity but must be labeled as such.
satisfying_stop: Produce the first triangular-square total above one million, and justify that the recurrence skipped no positive solution using a decreasing inverse with a base case.

title: Choose a rule that never loses a symbol
core_gate: Two-bit addition, distributive multiplication and inverse reasoning. The field claim uses the supplied polynomial-quotient ring fact plus a complete inverse classification.
index_gate: Bit coefficients, distribution and inverse proofs; field certification is algebraic
extension_gate: Linear decoding over a finite field; Frobenius extension uses polynomial substitution. No claim of the classification of all finite fields is needed.
assessment: Promising with explicit algebra gates; pair addition is accessible, while distributivity and solving a general two-report problem need preparation.
satisfying_stop: Derive every nonzero inverse for the successful rule and use it to prove that two distinct input-output reports determine a unique affine machine.

title: Which cube volumes can these tools reach?
core_gate: Exact compass/straightedge work is an entry. The actual obstruction requires rational polynomials, irreducibility of cubics, degree of an algebraic number and the supplied constructible-degree theorem.
index_gate: Field-degree theorem and cubic irreducibility; exact geometry is an earlier entry
extension_gate: Classify positive integer volumes; a separate angle-trisection extension uses a cubic cosine identity and irreducibility. Calculus is not required.
assessment: Advanced/specialist for the intended payoff. Exact square-root geometry is an accessible earlier stop and must not be advertised as the impossibility proof.
satisfying_stop: Prove exactly which positive integer cube volumes have classically constructible edges, using a stated degree theorem and a complete cubic irreducibility argument.

title: Move a corner, change the whole staircase
core_gate: Nonnegative grid coordinates, right/up reachability and a finite certificate for an infinite region. The quotient-basis stage needs polynomial linear combinations and independence.
index_gate: Infinite-grid boundary proof; polynomial spanning and independence for the quotient
extension_gate: Multiplication in a polynomial quotient and kernels of linear maps. A two-variable rectangle extension uses exponent counting and a proof of its basis.
assessment: First-pilot candidate for grid-ready learners at the finite-boundary stage; promising with linear-algebra gates for quotient dimension.
satisfying_stop: Find the unique legal one-step change that adds exactly two survivors, prove there are no other such changes, and, at the algebra gate, prove the surviving monomials form a quotient basis.

title: Can one calculation remember a rate?
core_gate: Signed rational algebra, distribution, polynomial evaluation and formal coefficient comparison. The value/derivative payoff needs polynomial differentiation or its formal power rule, stated explicitly.
index_gate: Rational polynomial algebra; derivative meaning uses the explicit polynomial power rule
extension_gate: The higher-order extension needs second derivatives and truncated polynomial multiplication. No claim about analytic convergence or actual tiny real numbers is made.
assessment: Promising with explicit polynomial-algebra gates; advanced/specialist when interpreting derivatives. Do not tell learners ε is an ordinary very small nonzero real number.
satisfying_stop: Use one exact dual-number evaluation to compute a polynomial’s value and derivative, then prove the general identity and product rule while identifying information it does not retain.

title: Encode a rational point with one slope
core_gate: Fractions, signed coordinates, substitution and factoring a quadratic with one known root. Exact symbolic algebra is needed for completeness.
index_gate: Exact fractions and quadratic factorization; completeness includes the missing point
extension_gate: Integer triples and coprimality/parity; an optional projective parameter handles the infinite slope. No general rationality theorem for all curves is assumed.
assessment: Promising with explicit fractional-algebra gates. The drawing offers a real choice, but completeness must be argued symbolically.
satisfying_stop: Derive mutually inverse point/slope formulas for every rational point on the ellipse except one, then explicitly include the exceptional basepoint.

title: Can these finite points make one cycle?
core_gate: Modulo-five arithmetic and a complete square-residue search give the finite entry. The new cyclic-structure payoff requires field division, point-addition formulas and a supplied elliptic-curve group theorem.
index_gate: Mod-five inventory; projective coordinates and a supplied group theorem for point addition
extension_gate: Projective triples, equivalence under nonzero scaling, formal partial derivatives and nonsingularity are explicit advanced prerequisites. Orbit completeness and group-equation solving use modular reasoning.
assessment: Promising with modulo-five gates for enumeration; advanced/specialist for the elliptic group structure. No cryptographic-security conclusion is made from this tiny group.
satisfying_stop: At the finite entry, certify the complete point set. At the advanced gate, find a point whose repeated addition visits the entire projective set, then solve point equations through its cyclic labels.

title: Design the round when closeness begins
core_gate: Fractions, simultaneous updates, signed differences and geometric powers. Exact first-entry bounds use inequalities; weighted invariants and parameter classification are the algebraic core.
index_gate: Fractional updates and geometric powers; weighted invariants prove exact convergence times
extension_gate: Linear algebra for eigenvectors; real geometric-sequence limits for the full parameter classification. No differential calculus.
assessment: Promising with fraction/algebra gates. Marker motion is accessible earlier, but weighted limits and all-parameter claims need algebra-ready learners. Not classroom-piloted.
satisfying_stop: An exact formula and a proof of the first round meeting a tolerance, followed by a family of starting pairs designed to cross a chosen threshold.

title: Can you preserve area without preserving shape?
core_gate: Coordinate vectors, parallelogram area and signed arithmetic. The general proof uses perpendicular projection/dot products; inverse and composition arguments require 2×2 algebra.
index_gate: Coordinate area and orientation; projection and matrix algebra support the full proof
extension_gate: Integer divisibility and inverse matrices for the lattice continuation.
assessment: Promising with coordinate-area gates; projection/determinant and rigidity arguments are an advanced continuation. A grid count alone is not an adequate core proof.
satisfying_stop: A complete parameter design for area 1, exact inverses, and a proof separating area preservation from preservation of all lengths.

title: Choose bases that reveal what an arrow does
core_gate: Finite-dimensional vector spaces over Q, linear independence, bases, kernel, image and rank. The general theorem works over any field. This is an advanced linear-algebra investigation.
index_gate: Bases, kernel and image; independent source/target coordinates are essential
extension_gate: Composition and ranks for the two-arrow counterexample.
assessment: Advanced/specialist with a genuine linear-algebra gate. Arrow cards can organize the proof but do not replace vector-space prerequisites.
satisfying_stop: An explicit basis decomposition with killed, transmitted and unreachable directions, plus a proof that these three counts completely classify one linear arrow under independent bases.

title: Find what commutes, then explain the cancellations
core_gate: Rational 2×2 matrix multiplication, subtraction and symbolic algebra. General identities require distributivity and associativity of multiplication, not assumptions about associativity of the bracket.
index_gate: Matrix multiplication and symbolic cancellation; a concrete test leads to general identities
extension_gate: Trace in arbitrary finite dimension for the operator obstruction.
assessment: Advanced/specialist. Exact matrix trials are meaningful learner choices for those with the algebra gate; they are not advertised as an elementary movement substitute.
satisfying_stop: A complete commuting-partner family, a concrete nonassociativity witness and a general Jacobi proof by cancellation of ordered triple products.

title: Make a catalog that remembers every choice
core_gate: Named objects, ordered pairs and compatible assignments. The universal-property proof needs functions and separate existence/uniqueness arguments; it can be explained with tokens before formal notation.
index_gate: Named pairs and matching colors; function uniqueness is the categorical continuation
extension_gate: Finite counting and fiber sizes for the projection/count extension.
assessment: First-pilot candidate for the finite catalog; promising with function-language gates for the universal proof. The counted catalog alone is not the full categorical destination.
satisfying_stop: A complete compatible-pair catalog and a proof that every compatible assignment has exactly one record-preserving map into it; duplicate records then explain failure of uniqueness.

title: Which face cards erase the same edge pattern?
core_gate: Parity, edge toggles and a completeness argument. Formal homology uses F2 vector spaces, boundary maps and quotients; the finite reachability proof can precede that notation.
index_gate: Even-degree edge patterns; vector spaces and quotient classes form the formal continuation
extension_gate: Kernel in degree 2 for a supplied cap-face extension.
assessment: First-pilot candidate for parity-ready learners at the finite game; the matrix/quotient continuation has an honest linear-algebra gate. No general topological-invariance claim is inferred.
satisfying_stop: A complete classification by two preserved outer-edge marks, with constructive erasing sequences and a minimum face-card purchase proof.

title: How much free space completes this module?
core_gate: Finite-dimensional rational vector spaces, ring/module action, direct sums and isomorphism. Projective means a direct summand of a finite free module here. Counters alone are only a preparatory model.
index_gate: Vector spaces and module actions; idempotents justify the two-inventory model of K0
extension_gate: Abstract commutative monoids and cancellation for the warning example.
assessment: Advanced/specialist. Paired counters faithfully represent isomorphism classes only after the idempotent/module argument. The hard gate is preserved rather than hidden.
satisfying_stop: An explicit smallest free complement and a justified computation K0(Q×Q)=Z², including a nonfree projective and a virtual class not represented by an actual module.

title: Count necklaces when every bead count is fixed
core_gate: Arranging six beads, exact counting and rotation equivalence. The fixed-pair proof needs orbit/stabilizer reasoning, introduced concretely. The n-bead formula uses gcd and binomial coefficients.
index_gate: Rotation classes and exact counting; the general formula uses gcd and fixed-pair reasoning
extension_gate: Gcd/divisibility for equal-sized orbits at coprime bead counts.
assessment: First-pilot candidate for the six-bead catalog and symmetry explanation; the general n,r formula has an explicit counting/gcd gate. Not classroom-piloted.
satisfying_stop: A complete fixed-weight necklace catalog, a proof of the rotation average and a real example where adding reflections merges two previously different types.

title: Can a box keep a secret?
core_gate: Spatial reasoning: keep three room axes fixed, follow and reverse quarter-turns, compare two marked directions. No arithmetic is required for the physical counterexample. Signed coordinates support recording; proving shortest length needs a small exhaustive case split.
index_gate: Fixed-axis spatial tracking; shortest-word proof; no arithmetic needed
extension_gate: Matrix multiplication for the optional complete commuting-powers classification; derivatives are required for any Lie algebra continuation, which is not assigned here.
assessment: First-pilot candidate with careful physical demonstration. The hidden-orientation task is stronger than merely seeing two different arrows. Spatial load is real; supply a partner recorder and allow three-face checking.
satisfying_stop: A witnessed order-sensitive pair, followed by a shortest three-turn word that restores the blue direction while changing the red direction.

title: Design a fence that defeats a match
core_gate: Compare heights and track opposite points moving continuously. The satisfying proof requires reasoning about every intermediate position and the half-turn exchange. Exact crossing locations are a separate fractions/linear-interpolation continuation.
index_gate: Height comparison and continuity; exact fractions are optional
extension_gate: Signed fractions for all ramp crossings or bisection error bounds. The real-analysis justification may use the intermediate value theorem; no higher-dimensional theorem is claimed.
assessment: First-pilot candidate for the core comparison argument, with close attention to opposite spacing and the seam. The exact fractions page is optional; doing its arithmetic is not the payoff.
satisfying_stop: A learner’s own attempted counterexample leads to the argument that a continuous height difference changes sign when opposite markers exchange places.

title: A cover with a tiny budget
core_gate: Halves, interval length, and geometric sums; the satisfying core includes an infinite list with a rule for its nth member. Finite paper play alone does not establish zero length.
index_gate: Fractions, geometric sums, and reasoning about an infinite list
extension_gate: Enumerating fractions and distinguishing dense from all points for the rational-number continuation. The interval-cover lower bound is supplied explicitly, not proved by a picture.
assessment: Promising with specific gates: finite entry is easy but the actual theorem requires geometric-series and infinite-list reasoning. Strong mathematical payoff for prepared learners; do not market paper cutting as a complete K–5 version.
satisfying_stop: A rule that covers every named point within any requested positive budget, followed by the surprising application to a dense list of rational numbers.

title: A root takes a journey
core_gate: Track and halve a running angle, including turns beyond 360°, and reason about a continuous choice between two separated alternatives. Complex notation is optional for the circle model but the no-jump argument is essential.
index_gate: Half angles and continuous choices; complex notation optional
extension_gate: Complex division and continuity for the formal ratio proof; integer multiplication for mth-root circuits. No unrestricted monodromy theorem is assigned.
assessment: Promising with specific gates. Dials provide real exploration, but some learners need prolonged practice distinguishing target, both candidate roots and tracked root. Finite checkpoints alone cannot establish continuity.
satisfying_stop: A one-circuit obstruction justified for every continuous choice, and a parity rule for routes specified by a continuous running angle.

title: Can a network hide a high point?
core_gate: Averages of two or three numbers, including halves, and reasoning from a largest value. Solving the shortcut network can use simultaneous equations or balancing; the core proof needs all averaging rules to hold at once.
index_gate: Averages and halves; proof by following a maximum through a graph
extension_gate: Subtracting two complete assignments for uniqueness and boundary sensitivity. The continuum harmonic-function connection requires analysis and is not proved here.
assessment: First-pilot candidate for average-ready learners. The shortcut makes the network choice consequential; uniqueness is a separate proof continuation. Signed differences and fractions need adult support for some learners.
satisfying_stop: A solved shortcut network and a proof that any finite averaging network with a fixed boundary in each connected component cannot hide a new maximum.

title: What does a real picture miss?
core_gate: Complex arithmetic including i²=−1, factorization, and two complex coordinates. The core payoff is an exhaustive solution set with two branches and a proof that a real slice can conceal almost all solutions. This is not an elementary-age activity.
index_gate: Complex arithmetic and factorization; four-real-dimensional reasoning
extension_gate: Continuity for the no-branch-switch proof; a supplied necessary local-disc condition for the optional complex-curve singularity proof. No calculus is needed for the explicit uv=c parameterizations.
assessment: Advanced/specialist. The algebra choices are genuine and the real-slice surprise is substantial. A four-real-dimensional object cannot be faithfully supplied as an ordinary crossing drawing; the paired diagrams are deliberately honest.
satisfying_stop: All solutions are parameterized and distinguished from their real slice; a later change of coordinates exposes why the zero equation has two branches while the constant-one equation does not split that way.

title: Build an angle machine
core_gate: Cosine as a unit-circle horizontal coordinate, signed fractions, and polynomial algebra. The satisfying proof uses cosine addition identities or their supplied symmetric form; finite numerical checks alone do not prove the machine works.
index_gate: Polynomial algebra, unit-circle cosine, and cosine addition
extension_gate: Polynomial composition and the fact that a nonzero polynomial has finitely many roots for the all-real composition identity. No calculus or approximation-theory theorem is assigned.
assessment: Promising with specific algebra/trigonometry gates. The choice of informative versus redundant tests and the false-candidate challenge are substantive; circle measuring alone is not the core investigation.
satisfying_stop: An invented triple-angle polynomial with a proof for every real angle, followed by a composition rule that connects angle multiplication to polynomial substitution.

title: Can a rate law choose a future?
core_gate: Calculus is essential: derivatives of powers, one-sided difference quotients at a join, square roots, and the meaning of a differential equation at every time. A sketch or slope game alone is not the satisfying investigation.
index_gate: Calculus required: derivatives, piecewise joins, and square roots
extension_gate: Chain and product rules plus monotonicity for the complete classification and comparison equation. Local Lipschitz continuity is defined on the final page; its uniqueness theorem is discussed as a supplied result, not proved here.
assessment: Advanced/specialist, explicitly calculus-gated in accordance with user feedback. The freedom to choose a waiting time is a real solution choice, and the join check is indispensable. Classification strengthens the counterexample without disguising its prerequisites.
satisfying_stop: At least two fully checked different solutions with identical initial data, including a chosen delayed departure and its differentiability at the join. The advanced continuation classifies every nonnegative solution.

title: Choose a shape, then choose its future
core_gate: Calculus is the core: partial derivatives, sine/cosine and exponentials. Graph sliding is an entry, not a proof of a PDE.
index_gate: Partial derivatives, trigonometry and exponentials; calculus is the core
extension_gate: Energy comparison uses definite integrals and integration by parts.
assessment: Advanced/specialist. Strong for learners already comfortable with derivatives; moving a graph alone is not a satisfying substitute for the mathematical core. Unpiloted.
satisfying_stop: Two distinct fixed-end wave futures with the same initial shape, plus the derivative calculation explaining what initial velocity adds.

title: Program the folded interval
core_gate: Fractions, a two-piece function, affine composition and solving a linear equation. The complete period argument needs symbolic reasoning.
index_gate: Fractions, affine composition and a proof about repeating words
extension_gate: General word counts use divisors and a finite recurrence; no theorem about chaos is assumed.
assessment: Promising with specific gates. Backward composition can be a substantial algebra step. Exact orbit construction is satisfying; a few irregular dots are not evidence of chaos. Unpiloted.
satisfying_stop: An engineered orbit and a proof of its least period; the later complete four-step inventory is a stronger destination.

title: Can tiny payments break a budget?
core_gate: Fractions, powers of two and comparing groups of terms. The core payoff requires reasoning about every proposed finite target.
index_gate: Fractions, doubling and a rule that defeats every finite target
extension_gate: Comparing ordinary convergence with averages of partial sums needs sequence limits.
assessment: First-pilot candidate for fraction-ready learners, with the infinite proof as the real gate. Avoid turning the launch into lengthy common-denominator arithmetic. Unpiloted.
satisfying_stop: A block construction that beats an arbitrary budget, contrasted with an exact geometric remainder.

title: How narrow can the error band be?
core_gate: Graphs, signed fractions, affine formulas and inequalities. No calculus is needed for the complete minimax proof.
index_gate: Graphs, signed fractions, affine formulas and inequalities
extension_gate: The general interval change uses algebra; best constants for continuous piecewise-linear targets use maxima and minima.
assessment: Promising with specific algebra gates. The movable-line search is concrete, but an attractive graph is not a proof. Unpiloted.
satisfying_stop: A global lower bound met by one line, with a uniqueness proof.

title: Choose a photograph that reveals the motion
core_gate: Quarter turns, fractions and trigonometric periodicity. Classifying aliases uses integer remainders; the final obstruction uses elementary polynomials.
index_gate: Fractions, rotating angles, periodicity and integer remainders
extension_gate: An ideal irrational-time observation uses irrational numbers and exact full-arrow positions.
assessment: Promising with specific gates. Arrow play is accessible; complete classifications require modular and trigonometric reasoning. Exact-time results do not claim robustness under real measurement noise. Unpiloted.
satisfying_stop: A chosen extra time that distinguishes two candidate motions, with an exact statement of what ambiguity remains.

title: Decode a picture from four sign patterns
core_gate: Signed addition, fractions and four-entry arrays. The basis proof uses dot products or their equivalent weighted sums.
index_gate: Signed arithmetic, four-entry arrays and weighted-sum cancellation
extension_gate: Three binary coordinates and parity for the eight-pattern extension.
assessment: First-pilot candidate for learners ready for signed quantities and halves; the full arbitrary-vector proof is a real later gate. Counters should support cancellation rather than imply that all coefficients must be nonnegative. Unpiloted.
satisfying_stop: A unique reconstruction of an arbitrary four-square picture and a predicted symmetry in its coefficients.

title: Predict what the sliding window draws
core_gate: Length, subtraction and piecewise graphs. The convolution connection uses the supplied fact that an indicator integral equals length.
index_gate: Lengths, interval endpoints and piecewise graphs; integral meaning is supplied
extension_gate: A third window requires definite integration and continuity of derivatives.
assessment: First-pilot candidate for the geometric core. A third convolution is an advanced calculus extension. The moving endpoint convention is the main practical risk. Unpiloted.
satisfying_stop: A full overlap formula explained by endpoint changes, with a successful inverse design from desired graph dimensions.

title: A graph feeds back its own mean
core_gate: Definite integrals, functions and linear equations are core prerequisites. Necessary compatibility must be checked again by constructing the function.
index_gate: Definite integrals, functions and linear equations are the core
extension_gate: The changed rank-one kernel uses a weighted integral moment; no general compact-operator theorem is required.
assessment: Advanced/specialist. The mean reduction is a strong surprise for integration-ready learners; graphs alone do not establish the compatibility condition. Unpiloted.
satisfying_stop: A complete unique/no-solution/family classification with necessity and sufficiency separately proved.

title: Choose what best flat height means
core_gate: Fractions, squared and absolute errors, and signed algebra. Rectangle sums supply the integrals; completing the square and a full piecewise argument are the core.
index_gate: Weighted rectangle sums, absolute values and algebraic optimality proofs
extension_gate: Finite weighted sums and expansion; Hilbert-space projection is context, not a prerequisite for the direct proof.
assessment: Promising with fraction and algebra gates. The unequal widths make the choice of objective visible. Unpiloted; use the first two pages as a complete investigation before the parameter classification.
satisfying_stop: Prove that the same landscape has three different best heights under three precisely stated costs.

title: Defeat a claimed derivative bound
core_gate: Calculus is essential: polynomial derivatives, maximum norms and quantified counterexamples. Fixed-scale graph sketches are evidence; the all-bounds obstruction needs exact derivatives.
index_gate: Polynomial derivatives, supremum norms and an every-bound counterexample
extension_gate: Forward differences, bounded measurement errors and a worst-case triangle inequality. The integration comparison on page 3 needs definite integrals.
assessment: Advanced/specialist. Calculus and quantifiers are the satisfying core. Small-looking plots alone would miss the point; the exact endpoint derivative and norm ratio make the result decisive. Unpiloted.
satisfying_stop: A polynomial construction defeats every fixed bound on derivative size in terms of graph height alone.

title: Choose a journey and its effort bill
core_gate: Signed speeds, durations, squares and algebra suffice for finite schedules. The claim for every continuous piecewise-C¹ path has a separate calculus gate and uses the fundamental theorem.
index_gate: Weighted squares for schedules; calculus for the proof over all paths
extension_gate: Definite integrals, endpoint constraints and equality in a nonnegative-square integral.
assessment: Promising for algebra-ready learners on finite schedules; advanced/specialist for the full variational claim. The cost is a mathematical rule, not an assertion about calories or fuel. Unpiloted.
satisfying_stop: An exact bill identity proves the unique cheapest schedule; adding a waypoint changes the winner in a controlled way.

title: A mirror that is too short
core_gate: Distances, equal-scale coordinates, reflection and the triangle inequality. The shortened-mirror proof uses a supplied strict-convexity tool with an explicit geometric justification; calculus is not required.
index_gate: Reflection and triangle inequality; convexity for a constrained optimum
extension_gate: Symbolic coordinates and a convex-combination argument covering all closed mirror segments.
assessment: Promising with coordinate and geometric proof gates. The first optimum is concrete; the shortened segment requires real abstraction and should not be settled by ruler precision. Unpiloted.
satisfying_stop: A global shortest route is certified by unfolding; when its contact becomes illegal, a separate argument proves the new endpoint winner.

title: Make a four-peg challenge
core_gate: Convex hulls as stretched bands, planar cases and a complete argument. Exact certificates later require fractions and coordinate combinations; general dimension requires a separately supplied linear-algebra fact.
index_gate: Convex-hull pictures and complete cases; fractions for exact certificates
extension_gate: Linear dependence in R^(d+1), signed coefficients and normalized convex combinations.
assessment: First-pilot candidate for the planar core with oral rules and drawings; the exact certificate and general-dimensional theorem have separate gates. Unpiloted; give time to understand one-point hulls before challenging the theorem.
satisfying_stop: A strategy works for every four-point arrangement, including collinear and coincident cases, while three pegs can defeat it.

title: Let the route turn a tangent arrow
core_gate: Three-dimensional tangent vectors and a precisely supplied great-circle transport rule. Following a ball is entry; signed vector tracking is the proof. Varied longitude later needs sine/cosine components.
index_gate: Spatial tangent vectors and component tracking; trigonometry comes later
extension_gate: Rotation composition, integer multiples of an angle and rational versus irrational periods.
assessment: Promising only with spatial-vector readiness; the trigonometric continuation is advanced. A hand-carried arrow is approximate and the exact rule must be rehearsed before interpreting physical results. Unpiloted.
satisfying_stop: An exact calculation shows every initial tangent arrow rotates by a quarter-turn around the octant; reversing or retracing has a different effect.

title: Test a reversible reshaping
core_gate: Tracing connected pieces and reasoning with a point-deletion invariant. The formal proof uses the definition of homeomorphism and supplied interval/continuous-image facts; arithmetic is not needed.
index_gate: Connected pieces and a point-deletion proof; maps are defined explicitly
extension_gate: Planar polygonal paths and a supplied finite-union-of-lines fact for a disk.
assessment: First-pilot candidate for tracing and puncture choices; promising with explicit topology facts for the proof. Physical string is an approximation to a space, so the one-point convention needs careful demonstration. Unpiloted.
satisfying_stop: A point-deletion contradiction rules out a loop-to-segment homeomorphism, and an explicit ellipse map demonstrates what a successful reversible map requires.

title: Find the flood’s joining height
core_gate: Signed squares, coordinate inequalities and explicit paths in a clipped square. Calculus is required only for the final gradient/Hessian interpretation, not for the exact component proof.
index_gate: Coordinate inequalities and paths; calculus only on the Morse continuation
extension_gate: Quadratic inequalities in x², path components, gradient and Hessian for a new double-well model.
assessment: Promising with coordinate-inequality gates; the Morse interpretation is advanced/specialist. Physical shading can hide a point connection, so equality at zero must be stated and used. Unpiloted.
satisfying_stop: Prove the exact joining threshold and all component counts in the actual square, then design the smallest water level for a forced crossing.

title: How much can one question guarantee?
core_gate: Fractions, comparing squares, and interval reasoning. Calculus is needed only on page 3.
index_gate: Fractions, comparing squares, and interval reasoning
extension_gate: Derivatives for Newton iteration; continuity and the intermediate value theorem for a root certificate.
assessment: Promising first pilot for fraction-ready learners. The adversarial search creates a reason to invent bisection. Use page 3 only with calculus-ready learners.
satisfying_stop: A best possible worst-case search strategy, an exact root bracket, and an explanation of its guarantee.

title: Find every shortest route around a cylinder
core_gate: Spatial unrolling and the Pythagorean theorem. Integer shifts support the all-routes proof; no calculus.
index_gate: Spatial unrolling and the Pythagorean theorem
extension_gate: Absolute-value comparisons for a moving endpoint; distance formula for arbitrary circumference and height.
assessment: First-pilot candidate for learners who know or can use the Pythagorean theorem. Physical string exploration has a genuine proof destination. Younger learners can compare routes, but the complete certificate uses lengths.
satisfying_stop: Two different shortest surface routes and a lower bound excluding every hidden winding.

title: Can every pair agree and everyone disagree?
core_gate: Ordering endpoints and drawing intervals. Signed coordinates and inequalities enter on page 3.
index_gate: Ordering endpoints and drawing intervals
extension_gate: Convex combinations and Radon’s theorem only for a later planar Helly proof, not required here.
assessment: First-pilot candidate. The strongest moment is replacing many pair checks with two extremal witnesses. The plane continuation is a new gate, not compulsory.
satisfying_stop: A two-interval certificate for every failure on a line, followed by exact counterexamples when hypotheses change.

title: Predict the cut before using scissors
core_gate: Tracing joined edges and counting circuits. No arithmetic beyond small counts; adult reading can help.
index_gate: Tracing joined edges and counting circuits
extension_gate: Reasoning about a repeated seam permutation for equal-width lanes. Knotting and linking are outside the classification.
assessment: First-pilot candidate with time for construction and surprises. Insist on a prediction and an explanation after cutting. One impressive demonstration alone misses the mathematics.
satisfying_stop: A flat seam proof predicting connected pieces, boundary loops and the effect of a center cut.

title: Where did the starting value go?
core_gate: Derivatives, integration by parts, improper integrals and elementary exponential algebra.
index_gate: Derivatives, integration by parts, improper integrals and elementary exponential algebra.
extension_gate: Partial fractions and the integrating-factor argument for uniqueness. No elementary replacement is claimed.
assessment: Advanced, calculus-gated investigation. A meaningful debugging problem, not merely a transform-table exercise. Allow a second meeting for the integral justification.
satisfying_stop: An initial value located in the boundary term, two different recovered trajectories, and direct verification in the original equation.

title: Infinitely many doublings before the deadline
core_gate: Calculus is the core gate: derivatives, rational functions and limits. Fraction work alone is a warm-up.
index_gate: Calculus is the core gate: derivatives, rational functions and limits
extension_gate: Separation or a reciprocal substitution; local uniqueness is stated explicitly when used.
assessment: Advanced, calculus-gated. The shrinking time gaps offer a vivid launch; the real investigation distinguishes uniqueness from duration of existence.
satisfying_stop: A verified trajectory with an exact finite blow-up time, and a proof that the other side of an asymptote is not its continuation.

title: Can four samples fool the average?
core_gate: Coordinates, signed squares and algebra for the finite identity. Circle integrals require trigonometry and calculus.
index_gate: Coordinates, signed squares and algebra for the finite identity
extension_gate: Second partial derivatives for the Laplacian; the general harmonic mean-value theorem is background, not proved by four samples.
assessment: Promising algebra investigation with a substantial calculus continuation. Keep the distinction between four samples and the entire circle visible throughout.
satisfying_stop: A complete quadratic classification, a counterexample to trusting one four-point test, and a circle-integral proof for calculus-ready learners.

title: Will feedback find the point that exists?
core_gate: Fractions, affine algebra and graph reasoning. Continuity and the intermediate value theorem are supplied.
index_gate: Fractions, affine algebra and graph reasoning
extension_gate: Geometric limits for convergence; completeness is discussed through an omitted-endpoint counterexample.
assessment: Promising for algebra-ready learners. The shared fixed point of settling and cycling machines gives a compact surprise. Graph play alone is an entry, not the convergence proof.
satisfying_stop: A fixed-point existence proof and a complete family of examples separating existence, uniqueness and convergence.

title: The same clue, a different experiment
core_gate: Counting equally likely labeled outcomes and fractions; distinguish a random selection from a deliberate report. No algebra is needed for the complete finite certificate.
index_gate: Count equally likely outcomes; fractions; distinguish drawing from reporting.
extension_gate: Multiply simple fractions or count a two-draw grid; prior odds and likelihood ratios are an optional algebraic continuation.
assessment: First-pilot candidate for a group comfortable with fractions. The protocol distinction creates the surprise; avoid turning the repeated-draw page into long simulation or presenting posterior fractions before learners filter the cards.
satisfying_stop: Two correct but different answers to the red clue, proved from the mechanism; then a complete two-draw evidence comparison.

title: How surprising are these labels?
core_gate: Choose subsets systematically, add six small scores and compare sums; fractions such as 1/20. The real reasoning gate is fixing the null assumption and actual assignment rule.
index_gate: Small subset counts and means; explicit null model and random assignment.
extension_gate: Understand the difference between a prespecified one-sided rule and a rule selected after seeing the result; paired randomization uses three independent fair coins.
assessment: Promising with explicit statistical reasoning gates. A complement-pair representation avoids twenty rows of repetitive arithmetic. “Unusual under this no-effect model” is the payoff, never “probability training is useless.”
satisfying_stop: A complete 20-assignment reference set and a prespecified tail count, followed by an explanation of why a different assignment design gives a different answer.

title: A very precise wrong answer
core_gate: Means of small numbers, counting equally likely draws, and distinguishing the whole target population from the draw bag. The non-identifiability explanation needs systematic reasoning.
index_gate: Small population means; distinguish the sampling frame from the target.
extension_gate: Weighted averages with known group sizes; no calculus or asymptotic theorem needed.
assessment: First-pilot candidate when averages are familiar. The two indistinguishable hidden worlds produce a genuine impossibility argument rather than merely saying “bias is bad.” Avoid repeated draws after the mechanism is already clear.
satisfying_stop: Two different hidden populations yield exactly the same allowed observations, proving that more restricted data cannot determine the full mean; an improved sampling design is justified.

title: Build a promise an interval can keep
core_gate: Signed integer addition and subtraction, closed intervals, fifths and systematic cases. Keep one unknown target fixed while the instrument error varies.
index_gate: Integer intervals and fractions; track one fixed secret across random errors.
extension_gate: Compare a procedure’s repeated coverage with what is known from a realized report; optional randomized interval procedures use a separate independent coin.
assessment: Promising with a genuine statistics gate. The width optimization and intentionally unhelpful 50%procedure make coverage tangible. The coin-rule page is optional; explain its purpose before invoking general confidence-interval terminology.
satisfying_stop: A shortest 80%translation interval with a lower-bound proof, and an explanation that coverage describes the random procedure rather than a posterior distribution on the secret.

title: When the tangent robot comes back
core_gate: CALCULUS: derivative as tangent slope, evaluating cubics, rational arithmetic and a tangent-line zero. The loop is a Newton-method investigation only with this gate retained.
index_gate: Calculus: derivatives and tangent updates; continuity for the safeguard.
extension_gate: Continuity/Intermediate Value Theorem and algebraic interval-width bounds for a safeguarded method; a supplied geometric-decay fact is enough for finite error certification.
assessment: Advanced first-pilot candidate for learners taking calculus. The safeguard gives more than a familiar failure example. Do not relabel tangent motion as a lower-prerequisite guessing game.
satisfying_stop: An exact non-root 2 cycle despite available roots, plus a modified method whose sign bracket shrinks by a proved factor.

title: How many rooms must a machine remember?
core_gate: Follow directed arrows labeled R/B, count red cards in triples, and reason that the current room is the machine’s only memory. Lower bounds require comparing histories followed by the same suffix.
index_gate: Follow labeled arrows; remainders; compare histories using common futures.
extension_gate: Two simultaneous remainder conditions and a six-state construction; a pairwise distinguishability argument proves minimality.
assessment: First-pilot candidate with low arithmetic requirements and substantial proof. Learners get construction and adversarial testing before state-distinguishability is introduced. Do not confuse passing several short tests with a universal proof.
satisfying_stop: A working three-room machine and a proof that every two-room machine fails for some finite string; optional six-room extension has its own lower bound.

title: Two motions hiding in one machine
core_gate: ALGEBRA: signed displacement coordinates, linear force formulas, proportional pairs and factorization. The complete static force-pattern classification is a real stop; paper movement alone is not the whole result.
index_gate: Algebra for force modes; calculus for oscillation and exact nonrepetition.
extension_gate: CALCULUS: differentiate cosine twice and verify a two-component ODE. Exact nonrepetition additionally uses the irrationality of √3 and cosine’s period.
assessment: Promising with algebra; specialist continuation with calculus. The classification and sum/difference coordinates give a strong mathematical payoff. Keep temporal frequencies and recurrence claims behind the calculus gate.
satisfying_stop: Classify the two force patterns and uniquely decompose any initial displacement. With calculus, verify the motion and explain why two periodic modes can combine into a motion with no exact common repeat.

title: Add a spring: softer or stiffer?
core_gate: Fractions and algebra with F=kx; distinguish shared force from shared extension. Proving completeness for three springs requires structural cases, not calculus.
index_gate: Algebra: force/extension equations, fractions and recursive networks.
extension_gate: Series-parallel recursive constructions and reciprocal duality. Continuum elasticity, material failure and non-series-parallel networks remain outside this core.
assessment: First-pilot candidate for an algebra-ready group. The complete four-response classification and series/parallel duality make this more than substituting into two formulas. Younger exploration of hardware alone is not advertised as the full mathematical result.
satisfying_stop: Explain the series/parallel reversal from compatibility and force balance; classify all three-unit-spring responses and certify an impossible target, then construct it with four.

title: What can a flow map actually tell you?
core_gate: Area, speed and volume units; multiplication, division and weighted means. Algebra describes every branch split. A storage ledger is the core conservation argument.
index_gate: Area × mean speed, weighted means and conservation; algebra for every branch split
extension_gate: Vector calculus and the divergence theorem for the local continuity equation. Density and mass-rate arithmetic for the compressible continuation.
assessment: Promising with fractions and units. The finite section/branch argument is a real conservation special case; the vector-calculus extension remains advanced. Physical model assumptions need explicit adult reading.
satisfying_stop: A conservation certificate rejects a map, while explicit distinct profiles and branch splits show what the same certificate leaves undetermined.

title: Choose the fastest crossing
core_gate: Pythagoras and distance/speed for the launch; derivatives and a global monotonicity or convexity argument are required for the satisfying optimum.
index_gate: Pythagoras and calculus: certify a continuous optimum and design its speed ratio
extension_gate: Implicit or monotonic comparative reasoning for changing a medium speed; no wave-boundary or diffraction theorem is claimed.
assessment: Advanced/specialist calculus investigation. The trial stage is accessible with roots and ratios, but alone is not marketed as a proof of the real optimization.
satisfying_stop: A unique global minimizing crossing, a correct boundary optimum when access is restricted, and an inverse construction making a chosen crossing optimal.

title: A dimmer signal, a hidden phase
core_gate: Signed waveform addition, sine/cosine and squares. The full investigation needs trigonometric addition and a two-coordinate representation; period averages are supplied explicitly.
index_gate: Coherent wave addition and trigonometry; use a reference to recover a hidden phase
extension_gate: Integration proves the supplied period averages; averaging over an explicitly uniform drifting phase gives an incoherent comparison.
assessment: Promising with explicit trigonometry. Pointwise cancellation is a useful earlier stop, but the phase-identification proof is the full core. Scalar same-frequency coherence must remain visible.
satisfying_stop: A complete brightness range and a deliberately chosen extra reference signal that removes a genuine two-phase ambiguity.

title: A sales pitch that balances energy and still fails
core_gate: Fractions, algebraic inequalities and a clear heat/work sign convention. The second-law entropy inequality is a supplied physical law, not derived from token accounting.
index_gate: Heat/work algebra with a supplied entropy law; certify losses and compare cascades
extension_gate: Reverse-cycle bookkeeping for a refrigerator. No microscopic derivation of thermodynamics is asserted.
assessment: Promising with algebra and careful model reading. Tokens support energy bookkeeping only; entropy and Kelvin temperatures remain actual supplied physics, not a “messiness” analogy.
satisfying_stop: A sharp bound, a reversible cascade achieving the same ideal bound, and an exact formula converting entropy generation into lost work for the specified reservoirs.

title: The question between two identical questions
core_gate: Normalized two-component vectors, dot products, squared probabilities and branch trees. The Born probability and projection-update rules are supplied as actual quantum model assumptions.
index_gate: Vectors and probability trees; measurement update first, optimal rotated basis later
extension_gate: Matrix multiplication for projectors; trigonometry for the optimal rotated basis and additional intermediate measurements. No complex-state or entanglement claim.
assessment: Advanced/specialist vector/probability investigation, with a compact four-state entry. Keep the Born rule and update visible; replacing them with an unexplained coin game would lose the actual mathematics.
satisfying_stop: Exact recorded-outcome statistics show an order effect, and an algebraic bound identifies the best single unrecorded intermediate basis for changing a formerly certain answer.

title: Build a sampler for a tiny magnet
core_gate: Four binary choices, complete counting and weighted probabilities. Distinguish the weight of one configuration from total weight of a class; arithmetic reaches 82.
index_gate: Four-spin configurations, weighted probabilities and an exact sampler; then ring parity
extension_gate: Exponentials connect the stipulated weights to Ising energy; binomial/parity algebra gives general finite chains and rings. No finite-system phase transition is claimed.
assessment: First-pilot candidate for confident counters, with fractions needed for the sampler and a later probability gate for rejection sampling. It is a genuine finite ensemble; the energy interpretation is supplied explicitly in the guide.
satisfying_stop: A first-spin/link encoding proves the weighted distribution and yields a small exact sampler; closing the ring reveals a new parity constraint and a corrected conditional sampler.

title: Choose a route for a clock
core_gate: Coordinates, slopes, squares and square roots. The flat-spacetime proper-time rule is supplied; algebra proves the finite piecewise-inertial comparison.
index_gate: Spacetime coordinates and square roots; verify the same clock times in a new frame
extension_gate: Calculus and strict concavity for optimizing the turnaround time at a fixed excursion distance. Curved-spacetime gravity is outside this model.
assessment: Promising with algebra and careful diagrams; the boosted-frame page is advanced. The main clock comparison preserves actual special relativity under a supplied metric, not a rubber-sheet analogy.
satisfying_stop: Design a specified elapsed time, prove the stationary route gives the largest possible proper time in the stated class, and verify the answer survives a change of inertial coordinates.

title: What can an orbit reveal about an unseen center?
core_gate: Algebra, squares, positive square roots and units. Circular centripetal acceleration and inverse-square gravity are supplied physical assumptions for the main inverse problem.
index_gate: Circular-orbit algebra, bounded-error certificates and an identifiable measurement
extension_gate: Trigonometric differentiation derives centripetal acceleration. A common unknown projection factor is a separately stated simplified observation model, not an inference from a picture.
assessment: Promising with algebra. The observation assumptions do substantial work and must stay visible. The exact/noisy/projected cases are separate pages, not silently combined into one misleading astronomy story.
satisfying_stop: A parameter is inferred with an exact consistency certificate; an explicit ambiguity is exhibited and a new measurement is proved sufficient to remove it.

title: Design a survey that can identify the depth
core_gate: Distance ÷ speed, positive square roots, fractions and two linear equations. The noise-design continuation uses exact interval bounds. The wave-speed law is supplied, not derived.
index_gate: Square roots and two linear equations; supplied wave model and exact travel times
extension_gate: Inequalities and weighted means for the effective-depth extension.
assessment: Promising for algebra-ready learners. The receiver-design payoff is substantial; this is not a physical tsunami model or an elementary substitute for wave equations.
satisfying_stop: A complete ambiguity family, followed by a chosen extra measurement that uniquely identifies both positive depths; an optimal receiver placement under an explicit error model.

title: Sell products, then price a proof
core_gate: Counting resources and revenue; fractions and linear inequalities for a price certificate. Whole products and divisible production are explicitly separate models.
index_gate: Counters and multiplication; fractions and inequalities for an optimality certificate
extension_gate: Piecewise affine formulas for arbitrary real resource capacities.
assessment: First-pilot candidate for fraction-ready learners. The counter launch works earlier, but the complete universal certificate needs weighted inequalities.
satisfying_stop: A feasible plan and matching universal resource-price upper bound, followed by an integer gap and a decision about which extra resource to buy.

title: Build a randomizer your opponent cannot exploit
core_gate: Fractions, independent probabilities and expected payoff; linear inequalities for worst-case guarantees. No general minimax theorem is required.
index_gate: Private independent sampling, fractions, expected value and linear inequalities
extension_gate: Positive real parameters and solving two linear equalities.
assessment: Promising with fractions and expected value. Playing is a launch, but short-run score averages do not verify the guarantee. The lower/upper certificate is the satisfying core.
satisfying_stop: Two independently sampled three-ticket randomizers with matching universal payoff bounds; an exact account of how deviations or revealed actions change the guarantee.

title: A fair copying rule can erase a color
core_gate: Independent sampling with replacement, fractions and finite outcome trees. Geometric tails and conditional averages for eventual-absorption proofs.
index_gate: Independent sampling with replacement; exact probabilities and geometric tails
extension_gate: Finite conditional expectations and a uniform absorption bound for arbitrary population size.
assessment: Promising with probability-ready learners. Copying has an accessible physical launch; expectation versus realized history is the essential conceptual distinction. The limiting proof is a genuine prerequisite gate.
satisfying_stop: Exact finite-time probabilities and a proof that eventual absorption has probability one, even while the expected count stays unchanged; an asymmetric three-parent fixation result.

title: Design labels that survive a reaction
core_gate: Counting and legal exchanges; signed linear expressions for all conserved labels. Integer intervals and a constructive path prove complete reachability.
index_gate: Counter exchanges, signed weights and a proof that every claimed state is reachable
extension_gate: Nonnegative integer states, enabling conditions and a second reaction network.
assessment: First-pilot candidate for the exchange launch and invented labels; general weights and reachability formulas need algebra. This preserves actual stoichiometric conservation, not reaction kinetics.
satisfying_stop: All linear conserved labels, a complete reachable-state chain with a legal-path certificate, and a second network showing why a conserved total alone can be insufficient.

title: Choose when one sensor can separate two tanks
core_gate: Fractions, powers and two linear equations; nonnegative real states. Exact bounded-error propagation and a geometric comparison for choosing the measurement time.
index_gate: Two linear equations, powers and nonnegative states; bounded-error sensitivity
extension_gate: A two-by-two matrix determinant and global observability versus exceptional states.
assessment: Promising with linear equations. Equal-rate ambiguity is accessible; the final timing proof needs powers and inequalities. Exact uniqueness must not be advertised as noise robustness.
satisfying_stop: A proof of permanent ambiguity, a complete positive-state reconstruction test, and a mathematically optimal observation time under a fixed absolute-error model.

title: Four messages through a damaged strip
core_gate: Binary patterns, counting disagreements and an adversarial guarantee. Powers of two through 32 and counting disjoint neighborhoods for the optimal-length proof.
index_gate: Bit flips, disagreement counts and a finite counting proof of optimal length
extension_gate: XOR parity checks, two-bit syndromes and a finite decoding proof.
assessment: First-pilot candidate. Concrete strips allow broad entry; the complete counting proof needs organizing possible received words. The staged supplied code is labeled honestly so a tested example is not mistaken for an independent construction.
satisfying_stop: An attained five-bit construction and a four-bit counting obstruction, with a precise separation between correction, detection and violations of the error promise.

title: Design a meter that disturbs the circuit less
core_gate: Supplied Ohm and node-balance laws, fractions and one linear equation; relative error and inequalities for a meter design. The entire activity is a paper DC model.
index_gate: Supplied circuit laws, fractions, one linear equation and relative-error design
extension_gate: Symbolic positive resistances and a two-resistor equivalent-source calculation.
assessment: Promising for algebra-ready learners. The branch diagram must be explicit. A physical voltmeter demonstration is optional future work; the present guarantees concern only the stated ideal model.
satisfying_stop: A correct loaded-circuit solution, a sharp resistance threshold for a chosen error tolerance, and a counterexample to treating agreement between meters as evidence of non-disturbance.
